## Pull request overview

This PR updates the repo’s shadcn/Radix UI layer to newer upstream versions, including migrating from the `radix-ui` aggregator package to individual `@radix-ui/react-*` packages, and adjusts sidebar styling to work with Tailwind 4’s limitations around `group-data-*` rule generation.

**Changes:**
- Replace `radix-ui` imports with direct `@radix-ui/react-*` imports across shadcn UI components and update dependencies/lockfile accordingly.
- Update button sizing usage (removing `icon-sm` / `icon-lg` variants) and adjust call sites to use `size="icon"`.
- Add explicit CSS rules + a Playwright e2e spec to validate sidebar text visibility when toggling collapsed/expanded in icon mode.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 53 out of 54 changed files in this pull request and generated 16 comments.

<details>
<summary>Comments suppressed due to low confidence (2)</summary>

**packages/plugin-view/src/ViewSwitcher.tsx:285**
* These action buttons moved from `size="icon-sm"` (32×32) to `size="icon"` (40×40). In a tab/header control this can noticeably change spacing and alignment. If you want to preserve the previous sizing, add explicit `className` height/width overrides (e.g. 8×8) or introduce a smaller icon size variant.
**packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx:1004**
* Row action buttons changed from `icon-sm` to `icon` (40×40). In a dense table this can increase row height/padding and reduce information density. If the intent is to keep the compact buttons, add per-button size overrides (e.g. `className` for 32×32) or reintroduce a compact icon size variant.
```
                              <>
                                <Button
                                  variant="ghost"
                                  size="icon"
                                  onClick={() => cancelRowChanges(rowIndex)}
                                  disabled={isSaving}
                                  title="Cancel changes"
                                >
                                  <X className="h-4 w-4" />
                                </Button>
                                <Button
                                  variant="ghost"
                                  size="icon"
                                  onClick={() => saveRow(rowIndex)}
                                  disabled={isSaving}
                                  title="Save row"
                                >
                                  <Save className="h-4 w-4 text-green-600" />
                                </Button>
```
</details>

`w-[--sidebar-width]` is not a valid CSS width value (it compiles to `width: --sidebar-width;`, which is ignored). This should likely be `w-[var(--sidebar-width)]` so the sidebar has a deterministic width when `collapsible === "none"`.

`className="w-[--sidebar-width] ..."` compiles to an invalid `width: --sidebar-width;` declaration, so the sheet width may fall back to `auto`. Use `w-[var(--sidebar-width)]` (or a concrete width class) to ensure the mobile sheet renders at the intended width.

`w-[--sidebar-width]` in this desktop gap element likely generates `width: --sidebar-width;` (invalid). If the intent is to use the CSS variable set on the provider, switch back to `w-[var(--sidebar-width)]` so layout and transitions work reliably.

`w-[--sidebar-width]` on the fixed sidebar container will emit an invalid width declaration. This can make the sidebar render at an unpredictable size depending on content. Prefer `w-[var(--sidebar-width)]` for the base width, and keep the explicit CSS overrides only for the Tailwind-4-missing `group-data-*` variants.

The expanded-state override for `.group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden` sets `display: block`, which can break elements that were intended to be `flex` / `inline-flex` via their own classes. Consider removing the expanded rule (and only defining the collapsed `display: none`), or changing the approach so expanded state restores the element’s original display rather than forcing `block`.

The slider no longer forwards `aria-labelledby` to the thumb (only `aria-label`). This is an accessibility regression for consumers that use labelled-by instead of a direct label. Please restore passing both `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` (or otherwise ensure the thumb gets an accessible name).

The dialog close button lost the larger touch target sizing (and the content is no longer mobile-first full-screen). This can reduce usability/accessibility on touch devices. Consider restoring a minimum 44×44px hit area for the close control and re-evaluating the mobile layout (or ensure the mobile-specific dialog wrapper is used everywhere dialogs appear).

Pagination icon buttons also switched from `icon-sm` to `icon` (40×40). This may make the pagination controls overly large on smaller screens. If you want to retain the previous compact look, add explicit sizing via `className` or provide a smaller icon button size variant.

Writing screenshots to `/tmp/...` is not portable across CI runners (and can collide between parallel runs). Prefer Playwright’s per-test output directory (e.g. `test.info().outputPath(...)`) or attach the screenshot buffer via `test.info().attach(...)`.
Same portability issue here: `/tmp/sidebar-collapsed.png` may not be writable/available on all runners. Use `test.info().outputPath(...)` or `test.info().attach(...)` instead of hardcoding `/tmp`.

This looks like a one-off local Playwright debugging script (hardcoded localhost URL/port, console-only output). To keep the repo clean and CI-friendly, consider moving it under `scripts/` (and documenting usage) or removing it from the PR before merge.

This appears to be a local Playwright troubleshooting script with a hardcoded dev URL. Suggest moving it into `scripts/` (with a short README note) or dropping it from the PR so the default repo root isn’t cluttered with ad-hoc test utilities.

Another ad-hoc Playwright debug script with hardcoded localhost routing. Recommend consolidating these into a single documented script under `scripts/` (or removing them) to avoid accumulating environment-specific tooling in the repo root.

This root-level Playwright CSS debug script hardcodes the dev server URL/port and is likely not meant to be shipped. Please move it under `scripts/` (or remove) and avoid assuming `/console/` is available at a fixed localhost port.

This comprehensive Playwright script writes screenshots to `/tmp` and hardcodes `http://localhost:5173/console/`. If it’s only for local investigation, please move it under `scripts/` (or remove it from the PR) and use Playwright’s test runner or configurable base URLs/paths.

This script is environment-specific (hardcoded localhost URL/port) and duplicates functionality already covered by the Playwright e2e suite. Recommend moving to `scripts/` with documentation or dropping it from the PR to keep the repo root focused on product code.
